vars.proof: I'm doing exactly this right now for a solar and electrical contractor in Arizona.
vars.offerGoal: where your jobs get stuck between signing and PTO
vars.offerWhy: I'm doing them now, before year-end, so you go into next year clean.
vars.tipFallback: start a 10-minute Monday review of every open job: what stage it's in and how long it's been there.

no-lead-tracking.label: Leads not tracked anywhere central
no-lead-tracking.tip: put every new lead in one shared list with a next step and a date, and review it for 10 minutes every Monday.

leads-in-spreadsheet.label: Leads tracked in a spreadsheet
leads-in-spreadsheet.tip: put every new lead in one shared list with a next step and a date, and review it for 10 minutes every Monday.

rep-owned-leads.label: Leads live in reps' phones
rep-owned-leads.tip: put every new lead in one shared list with a next step and a date, and review it for 10 minutes every Monday.

slow-lead-response.label: Slow speed-to-lead
slow-lead-response.tip: set up an instant auto-text to every new lead saying you'll call within the hour, and make same-hour callbacks a rule.

no-lead-metrics.label: No visibility on lead response time
no-lead-metrics.tip: log the time each lead came in and the time of the first call for two weeks. The gap will tell you a lot.

no-proposal-followup.label: Unsigned proposals go cold
no-proposal-followup.tip: follow up every unsigned proposal on day 2, day 5 and day 10. Even a calendar reminder for each one wins deals back.

inconsistent-followup.label: Follow-up depends on the rep
inconsistent-followup.tip: follow up every unsigned proposal on day 2, day 5 and day 10. Even a calendar reminder for each one wins deals back.

pipeline-spreadsheet.label: Job pipeline on a spreadsheet or whiteboard
pipeline-spreadsheet.tip: add a stage and a days-in-stage column to your job list and sort by days-in-stage every Monday. The stuck jobs jump right out.

key-person-risk.label: Pipeline lives in one person's head
key-person-risk.tip: add a stage and a days-in-stage column to your job list and sort by days-in-stage every Monday. The stuck jobs jump right out.

fragmented-tools.label: Job status split across tools
fragmented-tools.tip: add a stage and a days-in-stage column to your job list and sort by days-in-stage every Monday. The stuck jobs jump right out.

permit-delays.label: Jobs stuck in permitting
permit-delays.tip: keep a list of each AHJ's turnaround time and what they kick back most, and check every permit against it before you submit.

interconnection-delays.label: Jobs stuck in utility interconnection
interconnection-delays.tip: log the date each utility application goes in, and set a follow-up reminder 10 business days later.

pto-delays.label: Slow inspection / PTO
pto-delays.tip: request the inspection the same day the install finishes, and keep a waiting-on-PTO list you check twice a week.

customer-doc-delays.label: Waiting on customer docs / HOA
customer-doc-delays.tip: send the customer a checklist of every document and signature you'll need on the day they sign, not when you need it.

no-pipeline-visibility.label: No clear count of stalled jobs
no-pipeline-visibility.tip: add a stage and a days-in-stage column to your job list and sort by days-in-stage every Monday. The stuck jobs jump right out.

manual-status-updates.label: Status updates done by hand
manual-status-updates.tip: text every customer when their job changes stage. Even a template you send by hand cuts most of the where's-my-install calls.

reactive-comms.label: Customers have to call for updates
reactive-comms.tip: text every customer when their job changes stage. Even a template you send by hand cuts most of the where's-my-install calls.

rep-as-support.label: Sales reps stuck doing customer support
rep-as-support.tip: text every customer when their job changes stage. Even a template you send by hand cuts most of the where's-my-install calls.

wheres-my-install.label: Constant "where's my install?" calls
wheres-my-install.tip: text every customer when their job changes stage. Even a template you send by hand cuts most of the where's-my-install calls.

bad-reviews.label: Delays hurting reviews / cancellations
bad-reviews.tip: text every customer when their job changes stage. Even a template you send by hand cuts most of the where's-my-install calls.

wasted-trips.label: Wasted truck rolls
wasted-trips.tip: do a ready-check call 48 hours before every install: permit approved, equipment delivered, customer confirmed.

double-bookings.label: Double-booked crews
double-bookings.tip: do a ready-check call 48 hours before every install: permit approved, equipment delivered, customer confirmed.

material-coordination.label: Equipment not on site when crew arrives
material-coordination.tip: do a ready-check call 48 hours before every install: permit approved, equipment delivered, customer confirmed.

payments-spreadsheet.label: Payments tracked in a spreadsheet
payments-spreadsheet.tip: add a milestone-due date to every job and review what's due every Friday.

slow-collections.label: Deposits / milestones chased at month-end
slow-collections.tip: add a milestone-due date to every job and review what's due every Friday.

missed-milestones.label: Missed or late financing milestones
missed-milestones.tip: add a milestone-due date to every job and review what's due every Friday.

manual-commissions.label: Commissions calculated by hand
manual-commissions.tip: write the commission rules on one page and send each rep a per-deal statement when the deal funds.

commission-disputes.label: Commission disputes / clawback headaches
commission-disputes.tip: write the commission rules on one page and send each rep a per-deal statement when the deal funds.

design-only-tools.label: Design tool, but no ops system

generic-fsm.label: Generic field-service tool, not built for solar

double-entry.label: Re-typing data between tools
double-entry.tip: pick one system as the source of truth for customer info, and enter it there first, every time.

delayed-cash.label: Stalled jobs delay cash flow
delayed-cash.tip: add a stage and a days-in-stage column to your job list and sort by days-in-stage every Monday. The stuck jobs jump right out.

learn_q1.question: Question 1: how do you track a job after it's signed?
learn_q1.say: First one: once a job's signed, how do you keep track of where it is, through permitting, interconnection and PTO?
learn_q1.why: Whatever they say, follow with 'how's that working for you?' If they open up, hit Go deeper.

answers.label: In my head / my PM's head
Jobs get stuck and we find out late

opener.question: Permission-based intro
say: Hey, this is {{me}}. I'll be quick, and this is a cold call, so feel free to hang up on me in 30 seconds.
Mind if I take 30 seconds to tell you why I called, and you tell me if it's worth talking?
opener.why: Saying it's a cold call and asking permission lowers their guard. They get to say yes.

answers.label: Who is this? What's it about?

opener_pitch.question: Reason for the call, ending in a problem question
say: The reason I'm calling: I work with {{trade}} around Denver on the operations side, everything between a signed contract and PTO.
Something a lot of installers deal with: jobs move but the status doesn't. It lives in a spreadsheet or one person's head, and customers end up calling to ask where their install is.
Is that something you run into, or do you have that pretty buttoned up?
opener_pitch.why: State the reason in one breath, name a problem they'll recognize, and end on a question they can answer either way. Don't ask 'can I ask you some questions'. Ask about the problem.

opener_buttoned.question: "We're buttoned up": check the front end
say: Shops that have install dialed in usually still lose a few deals on the front end, with slow callbacks on new leads or proposals that never get a follow-up.
opener_buttoned.why: 'Buttoned up' on one side usually means the problem is somewhere else. Check the other half of the business before you move on.

opener_gatekeeper.question: Find the right person
say: No worries. I'm trying to reach whoever handles how leads and scheduling work there. Is that the owner or someone else?
When's the best time to catch them?
opener_gatekeeper.why: Get a name and a time. Write both in Notes.

answers.label: Got a name and a time, log a callback

opener_voicemail.question: Voicemail (under 20 seconds)
say: Hi {{contact|there}}, {{me}} here. I help {{trade}} in Denver stop losing jobs that stall between signed and PTO.
I had one specific idea for {{business|your company}}. I'm at [your number]. Again, [your number]. Thanks.
opener_voicemail.why: Follow up in 2 business days. Try 3 times max before moving on.

answers.label: Left it, log a follow-up in 2 days

lead_source.question: Where do most of your leads come from?
lead_source.say: Where do most of your new customers come from right now: referrals, door-knocking, ads, lead vendors?
lead_source.why: Paid and vendor leads are also sold to competitors, so how fast they respond decides who wins the job.

answers.label: We sub for other companies (no own sales)

lead_tracking.question: How are leads tracked?
lead_tracking.say: When a new lead comes in, where does it go? How do you keep track of it?
lead_tracking.why: If leads live in reps' phones, you lose them when the rep leaves, and you can't see what's falling through.

lead_speed.question: How fast does a new lead get a call back?
lead_speed.say: And when a new lead comes in, how fast does someone usually get back to them?
lead_speed.why: Leads called back within minutes convert far better than next-day callbacks. This is often the cheapest fix there is.

sales_proposal.question: How do proposals get built?
sales_proposal.say: Once you've got someone interested, how does the proposal get put together, and how long does that usually take?
sales_proposal.why: Slow proposals let a homeowner's interest cool, and the next installer quotes them first.

answers.label: A few days, back-and-forth with design
Reps build them by hand / templates

sales_followup.question: What happens to unsigned proposals?
sales_followup.say: Quick question: when you send a proposal and don't hear back, what happens next?
sales_followup.why: Stop talking after you ask. "Nothing" or "I try to remember" is the pain.

answers.label: Rep follows up when they remember

sales_close_rate.question: Rough close rate?
sales_close_rate.say: Roughly what share of the proposals you send end up signing?
sales_close_rate.why: If they don't know this number, nobody is watching the funnel.

pipeline_tracking.question: How do you track a job from signed to PTO?
pipeline_tracking.say: Once a contract's signed, there's site survey, design, permitting, interconnection, install, inspection, PTO. How do you keep track of where every job is?
pipeline_tracking.why: This is the core of the audit. Work moves but status doesn't, and that's where the money leaks.

answers.label: Our PM keeps it in their head

pipeline_stuck.question: Where do jobs get stuck the longest?
pipeline_stuck.say: Out of all those stages, where do jobs tend to sit the longest?
pipeline_stuck.why: Each stalled week delays the final payment. Find out which stage stalls and you know where to start.

pipeline_count.question: How many jobs are stalled right now?
pipeline_count.say: If I asked you right now how many jobs are in the pipeline, and how many are stalled, could you tell me?
pipeline_count.why: Not knowing this number off the top of their head is the 'owner dashboard' problem.

pipeline_impact.question: What does a stalled job cost you?
say: When a job sits stuck for a few extra weeks, what does that do on your end?
pipeline_impact.why: This is the implication question: it turns a process problem into money and stress. If they light up, open Go deeper and get a number.

answers.label: I end up chasing it myself

comms_updates.question: How do customers get status updates?
comms_updates.say: While all that's happening, how does the homeowner find out where their install is at?
comms_updates.why: Homeowners who hear nothing for weeks start calling, leave bad reviews, or cancel.

comms_calls.question: How many "where's my install?" calls a week?
comms_calls.say: Roughly how many "where's my install?" calls or texts do you get in a week?
comms_calls.why: Each one is 5–10 minutes of someone's time spent looking up status by hand.

crew_scheduling.question: How do surveys and installs get scheduled?
crew_scheduling.say: How do site surveys and installs get on the calendar? Who does the scheduling?
crew_scheduling.why: If the owner is the only one who can schedule, the owner is the bottleneck for every job.

crew_problems.question: Double-bookings or wasted trips?
crew_problems.say: In the last month, any double-bookings or wasted trips? A crew shows up and the permit, the equipment, or the customer isn't ready?
crew_problems.why: A wasted truck roll costs a crew-day. Owners remember these, so ask for a specific story.

money_financing.question: How are financing, deposits, and milestones tracked?
money_financing.say: On the money side: how do you keep track of financing approvals, deposits, and milestone payments?
money_financing.why: Financier milestones (M1, M2, PTO) that nobody tracks mean cash shows up weeks late.

money_commissions.question: How are rep commissions handled?
money_commissions.say: And sales rep commissions: how do those get calculated and paid out?
money_commissions.why: Commission disputes take up the owner's time and drive good reps away.

tools_current.question: What software runs the business today?
tools_current.say: What are you using to run all this today, software-wise?
tools_current.why: Write the exact tool names in Notes. You'll need them for the audit and the build.

tools_fit.question: Do the tools talk to each other?
tools_fit.say: Do those tools talk to each other, or is someone re-typing the same info from one into another?
tools_fit.why: Re-typing data between tools is a quick fix that's easy to show results on.

answers.label: Paying for stuff we don't use

owner_week.question: What eats most of your week?
owner_week.say: Last one, the big one: what eats most of your week?
owner_week.why: This is the pain they feel personally. Write down their exact words, because you'll repeat them in the close.

answers.label: Chasing job status / putting out fires

owner_one_thing.question: If one thing ran itself, what would you pick?
owner_one_thing.say: If one thing in the business just ran itself, what would you pick?
owner_one_thing.why: Their answer is what you sell the audit on. It shows up at the top of the pain summary.
